business: CollegeStat (collegestat.xyz): online help for Central Asian families whose child applies for a bachelor's abroad
target: Parents (and their 16-18-year-old children) in Tashkent, Almaty, Astana, Bishkek and Dushanbe planning a bachelor's abroad for the 2027 intake
where: Uzbekistan and Kazakhstan mostly, some Kyrgyzstan and Tajikistan; online, in Russian and Uzbek

segments.name: Middle-income parent aiming for low-tuition Europe/Asia (Germany, Korea, Turkey, Poland)
Upper-middle parent aiming for UK/Europe/Canada with partial scholarship
Affluent parent aiming for US/UK top universities
Student doing it alone, parents support but don't manage it

behaviours.name: Trusts a local agency
behaviours.how: Already talked to an agency in Tashkent or Almaty that is 'free' because universities pay it commission.

behaviours.name: Telegram researcher
behaviours.how: Reads study-abroad Telegram channels and asks in group chats before paying for anything.

behaviours.name: Price-sensitive, DIY
behaviours.how: Uses free tools (ChatGPT, EducationUSA, university sites) and pays only if clearly worth it.

behaviours.name: Ambitious, will pay for top results
behaviours.how: Considers premium consultants (Crimson-type) and wants the best chance at elite schools.

behaviours.name: Burned before
behaviours.how: Knows someone who paid an agency and got nothing; distrusts online payments and promises.

behaviours.name: Asks the school or teacher
behaviours.how: Relies on a school counsellor, English teacher or relatives who studied abroad.

behaviours.name: Busy parent, wants it handled
behaviours.how: Has little time, wants someone else to manage the process and report back.

objections: Local agencies help for free, why pay?
Is it a real company? We heard of agencies taking money and disappearing
A website can't replace a person who talks to us
Our child can do it with ChatGPT and free sites
We need help in Russian or Uzbek, the forms are English
Paying online in dollars is hard or risky for us
We don't know if the data is correct
It doesn't guarantee admission, so what are we paying for?
habits: you read Telegram channels about studying abroad most evenings
your child takes IELTS prep at a learning centre after school
you pay for most things by Click/Payme or Kaspi, rarely by international card
a cousin's son studied in Korea/Germany and you ask his family for advice
you saw ads from education agencies on Instagram
your child is in 11th grade and the school says nothing about foreign applications
